title: Practical Solutions to Common TAVI Complications
authors: Herbert Kroon
abstract: Aortic valve stenosis Calcific aortic valve degeneration mainly affects the elderly population. Approximately 15% of elderly patients have some degree of aortic stenosis (AS)1. Untreated severe AS will lead to heart failure, angina and/or syncope and approximately half of patients will expire within 2 years after symptom onset1, 2. Historically, open heart surgery was the only treatment for severe AS. However, advanced age was a dominant argument to defer surgery. Transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) was contrived as a less invasive alternative to surgery and to fulfill this unmet clinical need. After the first-in-human procedure in 2002, TAVI matured into a guideline recommended treatment of symptomatic severe AS in elderly patients across the entire risk spectrum3-7. Peri-procedural embolization Operator experience, improved planning and implantation strategies and multiple device iterations including smaller profile, repositioning ability and outer sealing fabric converted TAVI into a reproducible and relatively safe procedure8. However, the “Big Five” of complications in the modern TAVI era remain 1) access site complications and bleedings, 2) paravalvular leakage (PVL), 3) acute kidney injury (AKI), 4) conduction disturbances including the need for permanent pacemaker implantation (PPI) and 5) stroke9. Up to 5% of patients suffer a neurological event after TAVI, mainly within the first 48 hours8, 10, 11. This finding suggests a direct causative role with the transcatheter valve implantation itself. Transcranial Doppler and brain Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) studies revealed debris embolization towards the brain and new brain lesions after TAVI in the vast majority of patients12-15. Most of these embolizations remain clinically silent at first sight but may be linked to neurocognitive decline and frank dementia16. Embolic protection devices (EPD) have been developed to deflect or capture embolized debris on its way to the brain and may possibly reduce brain lesions and neurological events including stroke and neurocognitive decline. Part I of this thesis adds perspective to the etiopathology of TAVI related stroke and the mechanism of action of the current spectrum of cerebral embolic protection devices. We also present insights into the microscopic analysis of debris that was captured with filters during TAVI procedures. Vascular access and complications 1 TAVI typically requires large bore femoral artery access. By default, larger arteriotomies are at higher risk for access site complications and bleedings. A completely percutaneous approach relies on vascular access closure devices (VCD) to manage the arteriotomy and provide patent hemostasis. TAVI in low to intermediate risk patients is associated with a major vascular complication rate ranging between 2 and 8%4, 11. The conventional closure technique is based on sutures and most access site complications after TAVI procedures are related to closure device failure17. A collagen plug based closure device was introduced as an alternative to sutures. Part II of this thesis addresses vascular complications and provides information on clinical outcomes with collagen plug-based VCD. TAVI-related conduction disturbances Acquired conduction disturbances after TAVI are frequent and may lead to heart failure (re-) admissions and impaired long-term prognosis18-22. The atrioventricular bundle pierces the membranous septum between the right and non-coronary cusp of the aortic valve and surfaces along the left ventricular outflow tract (LVOT), which makes it vulnerable to contact pressure by the implanted transcatheter heart valve (THV) during TAVI23, 24. New left bundle branch block (LBBB) and third-degree atrioventricular block (AV3B) requiring PPI occur in up to a third and quarter of patients, respectively18-22. These conduction disturbances may be transient or remain permanent which is clinically relevant in view of in-hospital stay and overall healthcare costs. Unfortunately, there are no uniform definitions to describe conduction dynamics post-TAVI. Inconsistent reporting makes the interpretation of the literature on this topic challenging. Part III of this thesis will elaborate on what is currently known about the incidence of newly acquired conduction disturbances after TAVI and studies specific features on the baseline and postprocedural electrocardiogram (ECG) to predict conduction dynamics. These insights may help determine the need and timing of PPI and adjust hospital discharge policies.

title: Impact of cardiac phase selection on the diagnostic performance of CT-FFR: the role of myocardial bridging and heart rate
authors: Jianhui Song; Jie Zhou; QIYU ZHANG; FANG ZHANG; WEI GAO; YAN XIA; J Y Ma; Rende Xu; LEILEI MA; JUYING QIAN; CHENGUANG LI; JUNBO GE
abstract: Computed tomography-derived fractional flow reserve (CT-FFR) is commonly calculated from diastolic-phase coronary CT angiography, but phase selection may be affected by high heart rate and myocardial bridging. We compared CT-FFR derived from systolic- and diastolic-phase reconstructions and explored phase-related differences according to myocardial bridging and heart rate. This retrospective, single-center diagnostic-accuracy study included 138 patients contributing 155 vessels examined using a second-generation single-source 320-detector-row CT platform. CT-FFR was calculated separately from diastolic- and systolic-phase reconstructions using the same steady-state computational framework. Invasive FFR and CT-FFR values ≤ 0.80 were considered positive. Analyses of the invasive-FFR-defined grey zone (0.75–0.85), myocardial bridging, heart-rate groups (≤ 70 vs. > 70 beats/min), and subgroup interactions were post hoc and exploratory. Diastolic-reconstruction-derived CT-FFR showed higher overall discrimination than systolic-reconstruction-derived CT-FFR (AUC, 0.91 vs. 0.87; difference, 0.039; patient-clustered bootstrap 95% CI, 0.006–0.072). Diagnostic correctness did not differ significantly after accounting for within-patient clustering (OR, 1.18; 95% CI, 0.84–1.67; P = 0.346). In the invasive-FFR-defined grey zone, paired accuracy was 78.4% versus 56.9% (difference, 21.6% points; 95% CI, 4.5–37.0; exact McNemar P = 0.027). In vessels with myocardial bridging, the observed AUC was higher for diastolic than systolic reconstruction (0.90 vs. 0.79; P = 0.011), with an exploratory phase-by-myocardial-bridging interaction (OR, 2.72; 95% CI, 1.07–6.92; P = 0.036). In the heart-rate > 70 beats/min subgroup, no significant phase difference or phase-by-heart-rate interaction was detected. Diastolic-phase reconstruction showed slightly higher overall discrimination, whereas threshold-based diagnostic correctness was similar after accounting for clustering. Myocardial bridging may modify phase-related performance, but heart-rate-stratified findings remain hypothesis-generating.

title: Learning curve for transcatheter aortic valve implantation: a systematic review and meta-analysis
authors: Yang Zhang; Fanwu Chi; Ting Fan; Lian Hu; Yong Cao
abstract: Background Transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) is an established treatment for severe aortic stenosis. Although the procedure is technically complex and a learning curve has been described, quantitative evidence remains limited and heterogeneous. Methods We systematically searched PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, and Web of Science from inception to June 14, 2026. Studies comparing early vs. late learning phases were included. The primary exposure was case-sequence-based early vs. late program/Heart Team experience; calendar-time, volume-based, and device-specific comparisons were analyzed separately and were not pooled with the primary exposure. The primary outcome was 30-day/in-hospital mortality; secondary outcomes were moderate-severe paravalvular leak (PVL) and permanent pacemaker implantation (PPI). Random-effects meta-analyses (REML estimator), subgroup analyses, and sensitivity analyses (including HKSJ adjustment and adjusted-effect pooling) were performed. Results Twenty-two eligible studies (22 reports) were included. The primary case-sequence analysis included 11 studies and 30,690 patients; because of overlapping national registries, a reliable unique-patient total across all reports could not be established, and no summed total is reported. The early learning phase was associated with higher mortality (OR 1.99, 95% CI 1.52–2.62, P < 0.001, I 2 = 58.8%), PVL (OR 2.84, 95% CI 1.78–4.54, P < 0.001, I 2 = 53.0%), and PPI (OR 1.60, 95% CI 1.21–2.12, P = 0.001, I 2 = 0.0%). Exploratory subgroup analyses by the case-number threshold showed no significant interaction ( P = 0.163); these reflect study-level definitions, not risk during a specific case interval, and no specific threshold is recommended. The HKSJ sensitivity analysis yielded an OR of 1.98 (95% CI 1.45–2.70) with a 95% prediction interval of 0.90–4.35. Adjusted-effect pooling yielded an OR of 2.07 (95% CI 1.34–3.18, I 2 = 23.9%). No significant funnel-plot asymmetry was detected (Egger P = 0.136). Conclusions The early TAVI learning phase is associated with an approximate 2-fold increase in mortality risk. Due to observational data, temporal confounding, and heterogeneous definitions, the exact number of cases for proficiency remains undefined. These findings inform TAVI program implementation and training, but do not mandate specific case thresholds. Systematic Review Registration https://osf.io/u539h , doi: 10.17605/OSF.IO/CRNG3

title: Comparative real-world outcomes of LifeStream and Viabahn VBX balloon-expandable covered stents for iliac artery occlusive disease
authors: Yusuke Tomoi; Mitsuyoshi Takahara; Kenji Ogata; Tatsuro Takei; Yoshimitsu Soga; Kenji Andò
abstract: PURPOSE: Balloon-expandable covered stents (CSs) are increasingly used for complex iliac artery occlusive disease, but direct comparative data among CS platforms remain limited. This study compared 1-year restenosis and clinical outcomes between the LifeStream and Viabahn VBX CSs in patients undergoing endovascular treatment (EVT). METHODS: This multicenter retrospective study included 226 patients who underwent EVT for symptomatic iliac artery occlusive disease using either the LifeStream CS (n = 95) or Viabahn VBX CS (n = 131). Outcomes included restenosis, clinically driven target lesion revascularization (CD-TLR), re-occlusion, conversion to bypass surgery, and perioperative complications (POCs). Between-group comparisons were performed using inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) based on propensity scores. RESULTS: One-year follow-up data were available for 163 of 226 patients (72.1%), and 10 restenosis events occurred during follow-up. After IPTW adjustment, the balance of measured covariates was substantially improved. The estimated 1-year freedom from restenosis was 95.8% (95% confidence interval [CI], 93.1-98.6%) in the LifeStream group and 95.8% (95% CI, 93.1-98.6%) in the Viabahn VBX group, with no statistically significant between-group difference (p = 0.99). No significant differences were detected in freedom from CD-TLR (99.2% [95% CI, 98.0-100.0%] vs. 96.7% [95% CI, 94.3-99.2%]; p = 0.13), re-occlusion (100.0% [95% CI, 100.0-100.0%] vs. 98.1% [95% CI, 96.3-99.9%]; p = 0.091), conversion to bypass surgery (100.0% [95% CI, 100.0-100.0%] vs. 98.2% [95% CI, 96.4-100.0%]; p = 0.083), or POCs. CONCLUSION: In this IPTW-adjusted multicenter retrospective study, no statistically significant differences in 1-year restenosis or other clinical outcomes were detected between the LifeStream and Viabahn VBX balloon-expandable CSs. These findings should be considered hypothesis-generating because of the small number of events, incomplete follow-up, and potential residual confounding.

title: Carotid plaque morphology on computed tomography angiography associated with cervical recanalization strategy in acute ischemic stroke with anterior circulation tandem lesions
authors: Juan Ignacio García García; Ana Nuñez Guillen; Sonia Aixut L; Lucía Aja Rodríguez; V. Cuba Camasca; E. Ripoll Fuster; Mónica Cos Domingo; Oscar Sabino Chirife; Antonio López Rueda
abstract: Abstract PURPOSE To determine whether carotid plaque morphology on preprocedural computed tomography angiography (CTA) is associated with the cervical recanalization strategy used during endovascular treatment (EVT) of acute ischemic stroke caused by anterior circulation tandem atherosclerotic lesions. METHODS We retrospectively analyzed a prospective single-center database of consecutive adults treated with mechanical thrombectomy within 24 h of last known well between January 2022 and February 2025. CTA features of the extracranial internal carotid artery lesion included plaque composition, occlusion-cap morphology, string sign, and calcification pattern (none, eggshell, or dystrophic). Patients were categorized according to cervical recanalization strategy: aspiration alone or percutaneous transluminal angioplasty with or without stenting (PTA±stent). Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify factors independently associated with PTA±stent. RESULTS Seventy-nine patients were included (median age, 68 years). Cervical recanalization was achieved with aspiration alone in 40 patients (50.6%) and with PTA±stent in 39 (49.4%); stents were implanted in 14 patients. Dystrophic calcification was more frequent in the PTA±stent group (38.5% vs. 17.5%; p = 0.038). Dystrophic calcification (adjusted odds ratio [OR], 4.84; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.37–17.06; p = 0.014) and male sex (adjusted OR, 4.97; 95% CI, 1.43–17.31; p = 0.012) were independently associated with PTA±stent. Successful intracranial reperfusion was more frequent in the PTA±stent group (92.3% vs. 70.0%; p = 0.012), with no significant differences in symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage or 90-day functional outcome. CONCLUSION Dystrophic carotid calcification on CTA was independently associated with the use of cervical angioplasty with or without stenting. This preprocedural imaging feature may facilitate technical and antithrombotic planning during thrombectomy for tandem occlusions.

title: Micro-RNAs and Fibrosis Progression in Asymptomatic Aortic Stenosis: towards an integrated imaging and biomarker precision medicine approach to risk satisfaction.
authors: Jemima Osekafore Adewuyi
abstract: Aortic stenosis (AS) is the narrowing of the aortic valve. AS has a long asymptomatic period, during which progressive narrowing of the valve leads to pressure overload, resulting in adverse remodelling of the myocardium and fibrosis. Current guidelines recommend replacing the valve after symptom onset, but recent studies suggest the need for earlier intervention to prevent potentially irreversible damage. Therefore, biomarkers, used with imaging, could aid in providing a more appropriate time for treatment before symptoms appear. MicroRNAs which are small noncoding RNAs have in recent years been used as biomarkers for various disease due to their abundance and stability. This study aimed to identify novel miRs associated with AS and myocardial fibrosis which could be useful in predicting fibrosis progression and optimising treatment timing. A systematic review of the current literature highlighted the overall lack of data regarding miRs involvement in AS and myocardial fibrosis. Plasma was obtained from a cohort of asymptomatic moderate to severe AS patients to identify any novel miRs associated with fibrosis and progression. Initially, Next Generation Sequencing (NGS) was performed on a subset of the total baseline cohort (n=80). The analysis revealed miRs such as miR-451a and miR-21 were significantly dysregulated. Subsequently, the results obtained from the NGS analysis was validated in the entire cohort of patients (n=156) using RT-qPCR. The statistically significant miRs in the NGS analysis were selected to be validated in the entire cohort. miR-30e-5p emerged significantly downregulated in LGE-positive patients (p=0.01). In conclusion, this study has highlighted the significant roles that some miRs play in asymptomatic AS patients, specifically in the presence of fibrosis. However, for the progression of fibrosis, no significant miRs emerged.

title: Predicting cardiac conduction block in anti-SSA/Ro antibody-positive adults: development of a risk stratification model
authors: Xingli Gu; Zhaoxia Yu; Wen Wang; Meng Wei; Sicheng Xu; Xiaotong Liu; Lijuan Feng; Ruotong Cao; Meidina Yeerken; Xianhui Zhou; Baopeng Tang; Yanmei Lu
abstract: Background Anti-SSA/Ro antibody positivity has been increasingly linked to cardiac conduction block (CCB), yet the clinical features and risk factors for conduction abnormalities in this population remain unclear. Unlike degenerative conduction disease, antibody-mediated conduction dysfunction may be reversible at an early stage. This study aimed to identify independent risk factors for prevalent CCB at admission in anti-SSA/Ro antibody-positive patients and to develop an individualized risk-stratification model. Methods In this single-center retrospective study, 869 adult patients with anti-SSA/Ro antibody positivity were enrolled, of whom 174 had CCB at admission, and were randomly divided into a training set ( n = 608) and an internal validation set ( n = 261) at a 7:3 ratio. Lasso regression, univariate and multivariable logistic regression were used for variable selection and model development. Discrimination was assessed by the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), calibration by the Hosmer-Lemeshow test, and clinical utility by decision curve analysis. Based on the regression coefficients of the multivariable logistic regression model, the coefficients were simplified into an simplified risk score, and patients were stratified into low-, intermediate- and high-risk groups by the tertiles of the total score in the training set, missing values imputed separately within each set and all model parameters derived from the training set. Results Twelve variables were selected by Lasso regression, and multivariable logistic regression identified Gender (OR = 2.12, 95% CI 1.41–3.21, P < 0.001), Age (per 1-year increase: OR = 1.03, 95% CI 1.02–1.05, P < 0.001) and Heart rate (per 1-beat/min increase: OR = 0.99, 95% CI 0.97–0.99, P = 0.045) as independent predictors of prevalent CCB at admission. The AUC was 0.68 (95% CI 0.63–0.74) and 0.70 (95% CI 0.62–0.78) in the training and internal validation sets, respectively, and the corresponding Hosmer-Lemeshow P values were 0.9676 and 0.7584.In the internal validation set, the calibration intercept was −0.04 (95% CI −0.35 to 0.28) and the calibration slope 1.12 (95% CI 0.61 to 1.63). The odds of CCB increased stepwise across the low-, intermediate- and high-risk strata in both sets (intermediate risk: OR 2.54 and 2.80; high risk: OR 4.73 and 6.56, respectively). Conclusion Female Gender, Age and Heart rate were independent predictors of prevalent CCB at admission in anti-SSA/Ro antibody-positive patients. A risk score based on these three predictors stratified patients into low-, intermediate- and high-risk groups, with a stepwise increase in the odds of CCB that was reproduced in the internal validation set. Discrimination was nevertheless modest and, pending external validation, the score should serve as an adjunctive tool for preliminary risk stratification rather than for individual prediction or diagnosis.

title: One millimeter from disaster: multimodality imaging-guided TAVI in a young patient with restrictive aortic root anatomy—a case report
authors: Ata Firouzi; Amineh Safavi Rad; Mani Moayerifar; Mohammad Amouzadeh Lichahi; Maryam Jafari; Mohsen Maadani; Mahboobeh Gholipour; Golshan Ghasemzadeh
abstract: Familial hypercholesterolemia (FH) is a hereditary disorder characterized by lifelong elevated low-density lipoprotein cholesterol levels, which increases the risk of early-onset atherosclerotic cardiovascular and valvular diseases. Progressive aortic stenosis (AS) may develop early, further complicated by distinctive anatomical features of the aorta in FH, including a normal aortic annulus and a small supra-annular space, presenting challenges for percutaneous interventions. We present the case of a 37-year-old male with FH and significant comorbidities, prior coronary artery bypass grafting, liver transplantation, and carotid stenting, who presented with severe symptomatic AS. Due to prohibitive surgical risk, the patient underwent transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) with a 23 mm Sapien balloon-expandable valve, selected based on anatomical constraints. Despite the anticipated risks such as supra-annular squeeze, annular rupture, or paravalvular leak, common in similar cases, the procedure was successfully completed without complications. This case highlights the importance of individualized procedural planning and careful valve selection in FH patients with complex anatomy, demonstrating that, with an appropriate approach, TAVI can be performed safely and effectively even in challenging scenarios. The favorable outcome emphasizes TAVI’s growing role in managing younger, comorbid patients with contraindications to surgical valve replacement, though long-term follow-up remains essential to assess durability and ongoing clinical benefits.

title: Modified Supra-Annular Aortic Valve Replacement with Florida Sleeve Aortic Root Reinforcement for Aortic Regurgitation Associated with Behçet’s Disease
authors: Xianming Fu; Yangzhao Zhou; Xin-Min Zhou
journal: The Korean Journal of Thoracic and Cardiovascular Surgery
abstract: Patients with Behçet's disease who undergo aortic valve replacement for aortic regurgitation face significant risks of paravalvular leakage and prosthetic valve detachment. We describe a novel surgical strategy that combines supra-annular mechanical prosthesis implantation with Florida sleeve aortic root reinforcement. By anchoring the prosthetic valve to an external Dacron graft rather than the inflamed native annulus, this strategy aims to reduce these risks in patients with Behçet's disease and aortic regurgitation.

title: A calcification-modified Stanford classification for type B aortic dissection: anatomical features, post-TEVAR outcomes and prognostic associations
authors: Haoran Hu; Kaixuan Zhang; Ruimin Fu; Jing Qiang; Xi Yong
abstract: Objective Type B aortic dissection (TBAD) is a life-threatening aortic disorder. The traditional Stanford and DeBakey classifications focus on anatomical extent but do not incorporate prognostic factors such as aortic calcification (AC), which is critical in the endovascular era. This study aimed to propose a novel modified Stanford classification incorporating aortic wall calcification (the calcification-modified classification) and to compare the anatomical features, post-TEVAR outcomes, and prognostic associations of the resulting subtypes. Methods This retrospective cohort study enrolled 216 patients with acute TBAD who underwent TEVAR between 2021 and 2024. Patients were classified as Type B1 (no aortic wall calcification) or Type B2 (aortic wall calcification present) according to the proposed calcification-modified classification. Clinical characteristics, anatomical features, and postoperative outcomes including endoleaks, proximal aortic expansion (PAE), distal aortic expansion (DAE), and survival were compared between groups. All multivariable models were fitted with Firth's penalized likelihood to reduce small-sample bias. PAE and DAE were examined with a prespecified minimal adjustment set (classification and age; 4.5 and 3.5 events per parameter, respectively); persistent endoleaks were examined with fenestration reconstruction and classification (12 events per parameter); overall survival was examined with age ≥ 70 years, classification, dissection length ≥ 26.50 cm, and BMI ≥ 25 kg/m 2 (≈10 events per parameter). The incremental prognostic value of the classification over age for survival was assessed by bootstrap optimism-corrected C-index, the difference in C-index ( Δ C), the integrated discrimination improvement (IDI), and continuous net reclassification improvement (NRI) at 36 months. Results Type B2 patients were significantly older and had more prevalent aortic branch calcification, but less extensive dissection than Type B1 patients. Type B1 patients had higher rates of persistent endoleaks (20.3% vs. 6.9%, P = 0.009); fenestration reconstruction (OR 3.630, 95% CI 1.351–9.403, P = 0.007) and Type B1 classification (Type B2 OR 0.386, 95% CI 0.156–0.942, P = 0.022) were independently associated with persistent endoleaks. Freedom from PAE and DAE did not differ between subtypes (log-rank P = 0.981 and P = 0.161, respectively), and classification was not significantly associated with PAE (HR 3.208, 95% CI 0.597–18.357, P = 0.500) or DAE (HR 0.785, 95% CI 0.122–4.724, P = 0.876) in the penalized Cox analyses. The 3-year cumulative survival rate was better in Type B1 than in Type B2 (92.76% vs. 75.86%, log-rank P = 0.019); however, in the adjusted penalized Cox model, classification was not independently associated with survival (HR 1.922, 95% CI 0.837–4.936, P = 0.471), and adding the classification to age did not significantly improve discrimination ( Δ C −0.0096, 95% CI −0.0481–0.0088, P = 0.786; IDI 0.0125, 95% CI −0.0208–0.0657, P = 0.544; continuous NRI −0.0032, 95% CI −0.5208–0.2976, P = 0.612). Conclusion The proposed calcification-modified classification describes two anatomically distinct subtypes of TBAD: Type B1 dissection was associated with more extensive dissection, more frequent branch involvement, and a higher rate of persistent endoleaks, whereas Type B2 dissection occurred in older patients with a higher burden of aortic wall and branch calcification. In this cohort, the classification was not independently associated with overall survival and did not add significant incremental prognostic value over age. Its clinical utility may reside in anatomical phenotyping and endoleak-risk stratification, pending external validation.

title: Palliative Cardiac Surgery for Trisomy 13 and Trisomy 18 Improves Heart Failure and Facilitates Transition to Home Care
authors: Yûzô Katayama; Sho Isobe; Keisuke Tanaka; Takeshiro Fujii; Yuta Kawamura; Reiko Kawai; Shinichi Takatsuki; Kohei Ogata; Kotaro Hine; Kenichi Masumoto; Hitoshi Yoda
abstract: Abstract Background Congenital heart disease (CHD) occurs in 80%–90% of infants with trisomy 13 (T13) and trisomy 18 (T18). Although surgical intervention remains controversial due to limited life expectancy, palliative cardiac surgery may improve heart failure symptoms and facilitate transition to home care. This study aimed to evaluate the clinical profiles, surgical outcomes, and discharge rates of infants with T13 and T18 who underwent cardiac surgery. Methods We retrospectively reviewed 22 consecutive patients with T13 or T18 and CHD who underwent initial cardiac surgical intervention between April 2013 and March 2024 at our institution. Results The cohort comprised 22 patients (T18: n = 19; T13: n = 3). Primary intracardiac diagnoses were ventricular septal defect (VSD) in 12 cases, double outlet right ventricle (DORV) in 6 cases, patent ductus arteriosus (PDA) in 3 cases, coarctation of the aorta (CoA) complex in 1 case, and interrupted aortic arch (IAA) in 1 case. All initial surgical interventions were performed off-pump. At surgery, the median age was 25 [interquartile range (IQR) 16–30] days, body weight was 1.59 [1.35–1.75] kg, and median height was 41.0 [38.6–44.3] cm. Median gestational age at birth was 37 [34–38] weeks, and 14 patients had a prenatal diagnosis. Associated comorbidities included gastrointestinal anomalies in 7 cases, neurological conditions in 3 cases, and respiratory disorders in 2 cases. Serial measurements of serum B-type natriuretic peptide (BNP) levels demonstrated a statistically significant reduction postoperatively (preoperative: 736.5 [441.2–3316] pg/mL vs. postoperative: 164.7 [133.2–335.6] pg/mL; p < 0.05). Postoperative complications occurred in 5 patients (23%), including phrenic nerve palsy (n = 2), chylothorax (n = 2), and arrhythmia (n = 1). Overall, 18 patients (82%) were successfully discharged home (home oxygen therapy: n = 5 [23%]; tracheostomy: n = 2 [9%]). Two patients (9%) subsequently achieved definitive biventricular repair. Total overall mortality was 36% (n = 8), with a 90-day mortality rate of 4% (n = 1) and an in-hospital mortality rate of 14% (n = 3). Conclusion Palliative cardiac surgery in selected infants with T13 and T18 effectively alleviates heart failure and facilitates transition to home care. Surgical strategies should be tailored to individual family values and clinical conditions through multidisciplinary shared decision-making.

title: Case Report: Serial transesophageal echocardiography in atypical cor triatriatum sinister with dual-site left atrial thrombosis
authors: Chao Xie; Jing Tang; Chujun Wang; Wenjun Zhang
abstract: Cor triatriatum sinister (CTS) is rarely diagnosed in adults, particularly when thrombi occur in separate left atrial compartments. A 70-year-old man with recurrent atrial tachyarrhythmia underwent transthoracic and transesophageal echocardiography (TEE), which revealed a membrane dividing the left atrium into a main chamber and an accessory chamber. Multiplane and three-dimensional TEE delineated the membrane, its relationship to the mitral valve and left atrial appendage, and a suspected atypical pattern of pulmonary venous drainage. A mobile thrombus was present in the accessory chamber, with a second thrombus in the left atrial appendage. Assessment of transmembrane obstruction was qualitative; no marked flow acceleration was seen, but a Doppler gradient was unavailable. Catheter ablation was postponed because of the thrombi. The patient declined surgery and received anticoagulation. Repeat TEE 34 days later showed that both thrombi had disappeared, allowing ablation to proceed without a clinically apparent periprocedural embolic event. This case illustrates how serial TEE can establish the diagnosis, identify thrombi beyond the appendage, and inform the timing of intervention.

title: Multidimensional profiling of the early postoperative rehabilitation course after valvular heart surgery using unsupervised clustering: an exploratory analysis
authors: Ester Marra; Piergiuseppe Liuzzi; Andrea Mannini; Gaia Falorsi; Emanuele Buccione; Biagio Nicolosi; Simone Amato; Camilla Elena Magi; Paolo Iovino; Ercole Vellone; Joana Braga; Claudio Macchi; Hamilton Dollaku
abstract: Background Patients undergoing valvular heart surgery show substantial clinical heterogeneity that may not be fully captured by conventional measures such as left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF). Unsupervised clustering may identify clinically meaningful phenotypes. Objectives To identify data-driven clusters of the early postoperative rehabilitation course by integrating clinical, echocardiographic, and functional data, collected before and during inpatient rehabilitation, and to compare LVEF and early rehabilitation outcomes across phenotypes. Methods Patients admitted after valvular heart surgery were retrospectively analyzed. Principal Component Analysis followed by K-means clustering was applied to demographic, cardiovascular, valvular, echocardiographic, pharmacological, and functional variables obtained from medical history, admission assessments and in-hospital complications. Cluster selection was based on the silhouette score. Between-cluster comparisons were performed using non-parametric and categorical statistical tests with post-hoc correction. Results The cohort included 298 patients, of whom 59.7% were male, with a median age of 73 years [IQR=13]. Three clinically interpretable clusters were identified. C1 ( n = 72, 24.2%) showed predominant aortic insufficiency, preserved autonomy, and low atrial arrhythmic burden. C2 ( n = 117, 39.3%) was dominated by aortic stenosis, with greater cardiometabolic burden and greater wall-thickness measures. C3 ( n = 109, 36.6%) was dominated by mitral insufficiency, with more frequent mitral valve prolapse, higher atrial arrhythmic burden, and an altered mitral inflow profile. LVEF did not differ significantly across phenotypes. In complete-case analyses, Six-Minute Walk Test improvement showed a preliminary between-phenotype difference, mainly driven by greater gains in C1 than C2. Conclusions Unsupervised clustering identified three valve-substrate-associated clinical profiles. Our findings suggest that multidimensional profiling may provide an integrated characterization of postoperative heterogeneity and early rehabilitation trajectories after valvular heart surgery. Given the retrospective design, modest sample size, and complete-case outcome analysis, these hypothesis-generating findings require validation in larger prospective cohorts.

title: Pathophysiological mechanisms and evidence-based evaluation of extremely early in-hospital initiation of PCSK9 inhibitors in acute myocardial infarction
authors: Shihao Huang; Yujie Yan; Gang Pan
abstract: Historically, lipid management in acute myocardial infarction (AMI) has predominantly followed a statin-based stepwise titration strategy, causing many patients to miss their target lipid levels during the critical early risk window. Deeper research revealed that under the stress of acute ischemia and inflammatory microenvironments in AMI, PCSK9 exhibits a specific "extremely early burst", which impairs low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) clearance and directly drives pro-inflammatory macrophage polarization, endothelial barrier disruption, and microthrombosis through lipid-independent pathways. PCSK9 inhibitors achieve a dual blockade of this malignant pathological cascade by exerting strong lipid-dependent effects of lowering LDL-C and non-lipid pleiotropic effects of anti-inflammation and microcirculation protection. Recent clinical trials, including EVOPACS and EPIC-STEMI, substantiate that the extremely early in-hospital initiation of PCSK9 inhibitors (within 0-72 h of onset or periprocedurally during percutaneous coronary intervention) manifests a highly favorable safety profile concomitant with expedited lipid target attainment. Imaging studies, such as PACMAN-AMI, further demonstrated that early treatment can rapidly stabilize and promote the regression of vulnerable plaques, providing preliminary evidence that this strategy may reduce the short-term risk of recurrent cardiovascular events. Consequently, lipid-lowering pharmacotherapy is transitioning into a paradigm of "extremely early in-hospital initiation," effectively transcending conventional temporal therapeutic limitations. This review aims to systematically elucidate the stress-induced upregulation and pathophysiological mechanisms of PCSK9 within the acute AMI microenvironment, detail the dual interception mechanisms of PCSK9 inhibitors, and synthesize the clinical evidence base substantiating extremely early initiation over conventional therapeutic algorithms.

title: Extracellular matrix mechanical remodeling as a pathological switch: mechanosensing, disease progression, and therapeutic reprogramming
authors: Xin-Yi Qian; Yanwen Wang; Poh‐Ching Tan; Shuang-Bai Zhou
abstract: The extracellular matrix (ECM) provides structural support and mechanical signals that regulate cell behavior. Disease-related ECM remodeling can alter tissue mechanics and activate cellular responses that further promote pathological matrix deposition or degradation, creating a self-reinforcing feedback loop. This review compares ECM mechanical remodeling across chronic lung disease, cancer, arthritis, cardiovascular disease, and neurodegenerative disease. Although tissue stiffening is common in fibrosis and cancer, other conditions show regional softening or altered time-dependent behavior. These differences reflect tissue-specific changes in matrix composition and organization. Cells sense the remodeled ECM through adhesion complexes, mechanosensitive ion channels, and YAP/TAZ-related signaling, but the resulting effects depend on cell type and disease stage. Mechanical measurements are also influenced by the method and spatial scale used, which limits direct comparison among studies. Current therapeutic strategies aim to modify the matrix or disrupt abnormal mechanotransduction, but evidence that these approaches restore tissue mechanics remains limited. A better understanding of spatial and temporal mechanical changes may support more precise ECM-targeted therapies.

title: Endogenous Metabolite-Activated G Protein-Coupled Receptors in Cardiovascular Disease: Mechanisms, Evidence Appraisal, and Potential Drug Target Identification
authors: Nan Li; Weijie Yan; Shihao Fu; Zequn Yin; Yanxiang Wang; Yajun Duan; Zhenxiao Ma; 志伟 赵
journal: International Journal of Drug Discovery and Pharmacology
abstract: Background: G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) can recognize endogenous small-molecule metabolites and are important regulators of cardiovascular diseases associated with metabolic disorders; however, their comprehensive classification and translational value remain to be clarified. Methods: This narrative review synthesizes recent research findings on endogenous metabolite-activated GPCRs, summarizes ligand-receptor pairings for the various GPCR classes, analyzes downstream signaling pathways and the regulatory mechanisms underlying cardiovascular pathology, and evaluates the evidence supporting these receptors as potential drug targets. Only studies addressing endogenous metabolite-GPCR interactions were included; exogenous drugs and synthetic ligands were excluded unless used as pharmacological tools. Results: Metabolites such as short-chain fatty acids, ceramides, bile acids, and succinate interact with their respective GPCRs and are involved in cardiovascular pathophysiology, including blood pressure regulation, atherosclerosis, myocardial injury, and aortic dissection. Some of these metabolites can serve as diagnostic biomarkers, and intervention strategies targeting this axis hold therapeutic potential. Through structured appraisal of evidence strength, druggability, and tissue-specific expression, we identify SUCNR1 (GPR91), GPBAR1 (TGR5), and the ceramide receptor complex CYSLTR2/P2RY6 as high-priority candidates for drug development, with GPR35, LPAR subtypes, and hydroxycarboxylic acid receptor 2 (HCAR2, also known as HCA2/GPR109A) considered moderate-priority candidates. Conclusions: The metabolite-GPCR axis links metabolism and cardiovascular disease, providing new targets and approaches for its diagnosis and treatment.

title: GS-ECG: a generalist–specialist approach to structural heart disease prediction from electrocardiograms
authors: Jiacong Mi; Clarisse Florence de Vries; Derek T. Connelly; Honghan Wu
abstract: Abstract Structural heart disease (SHD) often goes undiagnosed, and echocardiography, the standard test, cannot be offered to every patient promptly. AI analysis of routine electrocardiograms (ECGs) could help prioritize who is scanned first. ECG foundation models promise broad applicability across ECG tasks, but SHD abnormalities are novel targets, defined by echocardiography and outside the labels on which these models were pretrained, so how best to use them is unclear. Rather than adapting the foundation model to these targets, we propose GS-ECG, a synergistic generalist–specialist approach that keeps it frozen and pairs it with a compact specialist, DGRNet, trained on novel SHD targets. In this setup, the generalist summarizes each recording in long-context features, while DGRNet focuses on SHD-specific waveform morphology at beat-level resolution, with a receptive field of about two cardiac cycles per feature. We evaluated GS-ECG in two health systems: MIMIC-IV-Ext-SHD (49,229 patients), a new public benchmark, and the EchoNext-Mini Dataset (36,286 patients). Full fine-tuning of the foundation model improved mean AUPRC by only 1.3–3.6% over freezing it, whereas DGRNet alone exceeded fine-tuning by 6.1–6.4%. Combining the frozen generalist with DGRNet in GS-ECG performed best, exceeding fine-tuning by 8.1% in both datasets while training 4.9% as many parameters; its composite SHD AUROC was 0.825 and 0.839. Against the published EchoNext-Mini Model on its own dataset, GS-ECG found 17–25% more patients with aortic stenosis, mitral regurgitation or tricuspid regurgitation among the top 5% ranked for echocardiography. Pairing frozen foundation models with purpose-built specialists offers an efficient route to clinical targets that lie beyond pretraining labels.

title: 3D bioprinting of tissues and organs for systemic diseases and localized injuries
authors: W. Kee Ng; Paulo Bártolo
abstract: Three-dimensional (3D) bioprinting integrates engineering, materials science, and biology to fabricate living tissues with precise spatial control. By enabling the layer-by-layer deposition of cells and biomaterials, it overcomes many limitations of traditional scaffold-based tissue engineering and offers new opportunities for regenerative and personalized medicine. This review presents a comprehensive overview of recent advances in 3D bioprinting. It introduces a systematic, ASTM-aligned classification of key bioprinting modalities, extrusion, jetting, and vat photopolymerization, along with their respective material and biological design requirements. It also summarizes recent progress in bio-ink development and crosslinking strategies that improve print fidelity and functional tissue maturation. In addition, the review highlights applications in both systemic disease modelling and treatment (such as cardiovascular, endocrine/metabolic, and neurodegenerative disorders) and localized tissue repair (including skin, musculoskeletal, cartilage, and bone), emphasizing their relevance to civilian healthcare and military medicine. By combining technological innovation, biological insights, and regulatory considerations, this review outlines how advances in multi-modal bioprinting and intelligent process control can accelerate the translation of laboratory research into clinically viable, patient-specific therapies, driving the next generation of regenerative medicine.

title: Clinical outcomes of apixaban in patients with atrial fibrillation and very high thromboembolic risk (CHA₂DS₂-VASc ≥5): a retrospective cohort study
authors: Abrar F. Alshehri; Abdullah S. Alshammari; Shaimaa Alsulami; Tamim N. Alkhaldi; Qussi H. Basranah; Saud A. Hijazi; Fatimah M. Hamdi; Saleh Alghamdi; Asma M. Alshahrani; Emad Elkholy; Mohammed A. Alnuhait; Mohammed Abdulrahman Alrashed
abstract: Abstract Background Real-world evidence on apixaban in patients with atrial fibrillation (AF) at very high thromboembolic risk (CHA₂DS₂-VASc ≥ 5) is limited, particularly from the Middle East. We compared clinical outcomes between apixaban-treated patients with CHA₂DS₂-VASc scores ≥ 5 and 0–4, and between prescribed doses within the very high-risk group. Methods In this retrospective cohort study at a tertiary referral center in Makkah, Saudi Arabia, adults with AF treated with apixaban between January 2019 and December 2024 were grouped by baseline CHA₂DS₂-VASc score. Outcomes were documented thromboembolic events, bleeding of any severity, and in-hospital mortality. Odds ratios (ORs) were estimated by unadjusted and multivariable logistic regression. A sensitivity analysis excluded patients with a recorded prior stroke. Results Of 596 patients, 175 (29.4%) had scores ≥ 5. Thromboembolic events (31.4% vs 7.1%; adjusted OR 6.6, 95% CI 3.9–11.0) and in-hospital mortality (14.3% vs 1.7%; adjusted OR 7.7, 95% CI 3.2–18.5) were more frequent with scores ≥ 5, whereas bleeding did not differ significantly (54.9% vs 46.8%; adjusted OR 1.3, 95% CI 0.9–1.9). Of 68 patients with a recorded prior stroke, 58 also had a documented thromboembolic event; after their exclusion, thromboembolic events no longer differed (5.2% vs 5.1%), whereas bleeding (adjusted OR 3.2, 95% CI 2.0–5.1) and mortality (adjusted OR 8.7, 95% CI 3.4–22.1) were more frequent with scores ≥ 5. Among very high-risk patients, prescribed dose (2.5 mg, n = 73; 5 mg, n = 102, twice daily) was not significantly associated with any outcome. Conclusions A CHA₂DS₂-VASc score ≥ 5 was associated with higher in-hospital mortality among apixaban-treated patients with AF. The excess of thromboembolic events was confined to patients with a recorded prior stroke and may reflect overlap between baseline history and outcome recording. Prescribed dose was not associated with outcomes, although dose appropriateness could not be assessed. Larger studies with complete dosing criteria and event timing are needed.

title: Risk factors for postoperative low cardiac output syndrome (LCOS) in patients with giant left ventricular valvular heart disease and its correlation with preoperative LVEF
authors: Wang Beibei; Zhenkun Yu; Ting Wang
abstract: To investigate the risk factors for postoperative low cardiac output syndrome (LCOS) in patients with giant left ventricle and valvular heart disease. Left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) was identified as a key predictor of LCOS. Accordingly, Pearson correlation analysis was performed to examine the association between preoperative LVEF and postoperative mean arterial pressure in this patient population. A retrospective cohort of 135 patients with giant left ventricular valvular heart disease admitted to our institution between December 2023 and January 2025 was enrolled in this study. All patients underwent heart valve replacement surgery and were subsequently categorized into the LCOS group and non-LCOS group according to the occurrence of postoperative LCOS. Baseline characteristics and disease-related variables were collected for both groups. Variables with significant differences were analyzed using a logistic regression model to identify independent risk factors for postoperative LCOS. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves and Pearson correlation analysis were subsequently applied to evaluate the predictive value of the identified risk factors for postoperative LCOS. Pearson correlation analysis revealed that preoperative LVEF was correlated with postoperative mean arterial pressure in patients with giant left ventricle and valvular heart disease. Among the 135 enrolled patients, 30 developed postoperative LCOS. The mean arterial pressure was (56.15 ± 3.76) mmHg in the LCOS group and (62.24 ± 3.81) mmHg in the non-LCOS group. Significant differences were observed between the two groups in cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) time, intraoperative blood loss, preoperative renal insufficiency, mean pulmonary artery pressure (mPAP), and LVEF (all P < 0.05). LASSO-logistic regression analysis identified CPB time, preoperative renal insufficiency, mPAP, and LVEF as independent risk factors for postoperative LCOS in patients with giant left ventricular valvular heart disease ( P < 0.05, OR > 1). ROC curve, calibration curve, and decision curve analyses demonstrated that the combined model incorporating these variables exhibited favorable predictive performance for postoperative LCOS. Pearson correlation analysis demonstrated that preoperative LVEF was correlated with postoperative mean arterial pressure in patients with giant left ventricular valvular heart disease. Multiple factors influence the development of postoperative LCOS in patients with giant left ventricular valvular heart disease, including CPB time, preoperative renal insufficiency, mPAP, and LVEF. Targeted clinical interventions should be implemented to mitigate risk and improve postoperative recovery.

title: Spontaneous lumbar artery rupture and retroperitoneal hematoma in a patient with postoperative subdural hematoma receiving rivaroxaban for atrial fibrillation: a case report
authors: Shuang-Long Xue; Ju Sun; Chen-Chen Zhang; Lei Li; Peng Zhang; Qi Yang
abstract: Spontaneous lumbar artery rupture is a rare, life-threatening cause of retroperitoneal hematoma with reported 7-day and 30-day mortality rates of 5.1% and 10.1%. Herein, we describe a 72-year-old female patient who developed massive retroperitoneal hematoma secondary to spontaneous lumbar artery rupture, only 15-days after evacuation of postoperative subdural hematoma and shortly after re-initiating rivaroxaban for non-valvular atrial fibrillation. The patient presented with severe right lower-back pain and hypovolemic shock, accompanied by a sharp drop in hemoglobin. Urgent contrast-enhanced computed tomography confirmed ongoing retroperitoneal bleeding, and transcatheter arterial embolization successfully achieved hemostasis. The patient recovered uneventfully, and complete resolution of hematoma was verified on 3-month follow-up CT. This case highlights the bleeding hazard of early resumption of direct oral anticoagulants following intracranial surgery and underscores the importance of timely imaging evaluation and endovascular intervention for this critical emergency.

title: Real‐world safety profiles of newer antiseizure medications: A pharmacovigilance study based on FDA Adverse Event Reporting System database
authors: Zimeng He; T Y Li; Yuyan Chang; Yang Liu; Minhan Song; Ying Zou; Chaolong Xu; Xiaofan Yang; Baomin Li; Fang Fang
abstract: OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to systematically evaluate and compare the post-marketing safety of four newer antiseizure medications (ASMs)-brivaracetam (BRV), cannabidiol (CBD), cenobamate (CNB), and fenfluramine (FFA). METHODS: A pharmacovigilance study was conducted using data from the FAERS database (Q1 2016-Q4 2024). Disproportionality analyses were performed to detect adverse event (AE) signals using three algorithms. Subgroup analyses were stratified by age, sex, reporter, and treatment strategy. We employed multivariable logistic regression, adjusted for covariates including age, sex, weight, dose, and concomitant medications, to validate associations between ASMs and specific AEs and to identify potential influencing factors. Bayesian network analysis was conducted to explore conditional dependencies among variables. Hospitalization risk was evaluated based on system organ classes. RESULTS: After data cleaning, 13 763 reports were included. We identified 308 positive preferred term (PT) signals. Seizure-related AEs were frequently reported. All four ASMs had the PT of seizure cluster, with each exhibiting distinct AE profiles: BRV with psychiatric disorders, CBD with gastrointestinal events, CNB with visual dysfunction, and FFA with valvular heart disease (VHD). Children had higher reporting odds of seizure with BRV and CBD, while reporting odds of FFA-related VHD were lower in children; polytherapy was associated with higher reporting odds of somnolence, and AE reporting patterns varied by reporter source. Both CBD-related gastrointestinal events and FFA-related cardiac events exhibited dose-dependent effects. Infection-related AEs were associated with higher odds of hospitalization for multiple ASMs. SIGNIFICANCE: This study comprehensively characterizes the safety profiles of newer ASMs and highlights the importance of tailored AE monitoring based on specific ASM and patient characteristics.

title: Development and validation of a dual-dimensional risk stratification model and nomogram integrating Naples Prognostic Score and left ventricular ejection fraction for in-hospital adverse outcomes in left-sided infective endocarditis: a retrospective cohort study
authors: Xinran Li; Lei Yin
abstract: Abstract Background Early risk stratification of left-sided infective endocarditis (IE), a severe valvular heart disease, remains critical for informing in-hospital prognostic assessment. This study sought to develop and internally validate a prognostic nomogram integrating the Naples Prognostic Score (NPS) and left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) to predict in-hospital adverse outcomes among patients with left-sided IE. Methods This single-centre cohort study enrolled 312 patients with left-sided IE admitted between 2020 and 2024. Independent predictors were identified using LASSO regression followed by multivariable logistic regression. Prognostic performance was evaluated via receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves, net reclassification improvement (NRI), and integrated discrimination improvement (IDI). A nomogram was constructed and internally validated via bootstrap resampling. Clinical utility was assessed using decision curve analysis (DCA) and clinical impact curve (CIC). Results In-hospital composite adverse outcomes occurred in 68 patients (21.8%). Higher admission NPS (per 1-point increment, OR = 3.01) and reduced LVEF (OR = 0.84) were independent prognostic factors. The combined NPS–LVEF model yielded improved discriminative performance (AUC = 0.839) and significant reclassification benefit (continuous NRI = 0.658, IDI = 0.061, both P < 0.001). The nomogram showed good concordance (C-index = 0.839), acceptable calibration, and favourable net clinical benefit in internal validation analyses. Conclusions The dual-dimensional NPS–LVEF model integrating systemic immuno-nutritional status and cardiac function improves early risk stratification performance for left-sided IE. This nomogram, built using routine admission variables, enables individualised prognostic estimation for research purposes. Given the single-centre retrospective design and internal validation only, external multicentre validation is required prior to any potential real-world clinical translation. Clinical trial number Not applicable.

title: Cardiovascular Disease Prevalence and Related Outcomes in Nigeria: A Critical Review of Evidence, Measurement Gaps and Care Outcomes
authors: Mary Ayodeji Olofin-Samuel; Temitope Grace Ayo-Oluwaseyi; Anuoluwa Deborah Odiru; Deborah Adebimpe Awolumate; Taiwo Folake OJO; Gentry Oluwabukola Ayo; Waleola Bukola Ige
journal: Journal of Advances in Medical and Pharmaceutical Sciences
abstract: Background: Nigeria is the most populous country in Africa and is passing through an epidemiological transition in which cardiovascular disease is assuming a larger share of adult morbidity, disability and premature death. Estimates of that burden nevertheless vary widely, and their reliability is rarely examined alongside the outcomes that matter to patients and health systems. Purpose and Scope: This critical narrative review appraises evidence on the prevalence, incidence and related outcomes of adult cardiovascular disease in Nigeria, covering hypertension, stroke, heart failure and cardiomyopathies, rheumatic and other valvular disease, atrial fibrillation, coronary heart disease, the principal cardiometabolic risk factors, and mortality, economic and health-system outcomes. Methods: Peer-reviewed literature and institutional reports were identified through structured searches of international and African bibliographic sources, supplemented by citation tracking. Studies were appraised qualitatively for sampling frame, case ascertainment, outcome completeness and analytical transparency, and the findings were synthesised thematically. Principal Findings: Hypertension is the dominant and best-documented condition, affecting roughly one in three adults, with a narrowing urban–rural gradient and very low population-level control. It underlies most stroke, heart failure and sudden cardiac death in Nigerian series. Stroke carries high early case fatality, and heart failure affects relatively young adults with predominantly hypertensive aetiology. Peripartum cardiomyopathy shows a striking concentration in the North-West. Coronary heart disease appears to be rising, but its burden remains uncertain because diagnostic capacity is limited. Much of the evidence is hospital-based, regionally clustered and methodologically heterogeneous, and population-level mortality data remain scarce. Unresolved Questions: True incidence trends, cause-specific mortality, long-term outcomes after stroke and heart failure, and the scalability of primary-care hypertension programmes remain poorly characterised. Implications: Priorities include a standardised national cardiovascular surveillance platform linked to civil registration and verbal autopsy, population-based stroke and heart failure registries, financial protection for chronic cardiovascular care, and sustained investment in primary-care hypertension control. Conclusion: The evidence supports treating hypertension control as the central lever for reducing cardiovascular harm in Nigeria, while emphasising that current burden estimates rest on fragile and uneven data.

title: Cardiovascular complications and cardiovascular death are rare in severe COVID-19 presenting with myocardial injury or failure
authors: Connor O’Brien; Fatma Güntürkün; Yaowei Deng; Ryan Ruaysungnoen; Donald D. Chang; Sameer Khanijo; Christopher F. Barnett; Shikha Kapil; Andrea Daly; Alberto Goffi; Dekel Stavi; Francois Carrier; Yasmine Ennehas; Babar Fiza; Andrew Patterson; Thomas C. Daubert; Vanessa Moll; Clara Castellucci; Mitchell Zekhtser; Nibras Burghrara; Michaël Mayette; Karl Courchesne; Shaun Thompson; Rushi V. Parikh; Juka Kim; Melanie D. Ashland; Paul K. Mohabir
abstract: Abstract SARS-COV2 infection has been linked to cardiovascular complications. Published data suggest that cardiac injury may be a common disease feature and contribute to morbidity and mortality in severe COVID-19. Since early in the pandemic, little data has emerged describing what cardiovascular complications arise from myocardial injury in severe COVID-19 and whether these complications contribute to mortality. We set out to describe the incidence and nature of cardiovascular complications in patients with severe COVID-19 infection and biochemical or imaging evidence of myocardial injury. We analyzed consecutive patients admitted for severe COVID-19 and presenting with biochemical or echocardiographic evidence of myocardial injury across 16 centers within the CARDIO-COVID investigator-initiated consortium. A light-GBM machine learning model was used to identify variables associated with mortality. Our study included 1,328 patients. ICU mortality was 29.4%. Factors most associated with mortality were age, SOFA Cardiovascular score, elevated troponin, intubation, high vasoactive-inotropic score (VIS), high PEEP, and high FiO2. Individual cardiovascular (myocardial infarction, stroke, pulmonary embolism, myocarditis, VT/VF, new onset heart failure) complications were rare (all < 5%) but common in sum (17.6%), and did not present significant association with mortality. Patients with high VIS and SOFA Cardiovascular scores had a significantly higher incidence of secondary bacterial pneumonias suggesting septic shock played a role in their physiology. Investigator-adjudicated cause of death data identified respiratory failure and septic shock as primary causes of mortality. Though cardiovascular complications of severe COVID-19 are common, they do not seem to contribute significantly to mortality. Elevated cardiac enzymes and myocardial dysfunction carry prognostic value likely reflecting myocardial strain in the setting of multisystem organ dysfunction rather than direct myocardial injury by SARS-CoV2.

title: Surgical treatment of a hypercalcemic crisis caused by a parathyroid tumor complicated by renal failure and cardiac insufficiency: a case report
authors: Qianqian Chen; Huiling Wang
abstract: The most common cause of hypercalcemia is a parathyroid tumor (PT). These rare tumors disrupt calcium and phosphorus metabolism and cause multiorgan dysfunction; surgical resection remains the standard treatment for parathyroid tumors. This case highlights the challenges faced in the diagnosis and management of patients with complex underlying conditions: for patients experiencing a hypercalcemic crisis complicated by renal failure and cardiac insufficiency, perioperative management presents a clinical dilemma between fluid resuscitation and cardiac tolerance, posing significant clinical challenges. A 61-year-old male patient presented with a hypercalcemic crisis caused by a parathyroid tumor, complicated by renal failure and cardiac insufficiency. He complained of excruciating pain in the lower back and extremities, polydipsia, polyuria, and constipation. Laboratory findings showed a serum calcium level of 4.27 mmol/L, an eGFR of 15.97 mL/min/1.73 m \(^{2}\) , and an NT-proBNP level of 1771 pg/mL. Based on these laboratory findings and clinical symptoms, a hypercalcemic crisis complicated by renal failure and cardiac insufficiency was diagnosed; imaging studies revealed a parathyroid adenoma in the right lower pole. Three months after parathyroid tumor resection, serum creatinine decreased from 340 \(\mu\) mol/L to 112 \(\mu\) mol/L. This case demonstrates that parathyroidectomy can be safely performed through the development of an individualized perioperative management plan based on multidisciplinary collaboration. The key lies in carefully balancing fluid resuscitation with cardiac tolerance, the appropriate use of diuretics, and the cautious interpretation of cardiac biomarkers such as NT-proBNP in the context of renal failure.

title: Two-dimensional speckle-tracking imaging for assessing cardiac dysfunction in liver cirrhosis: correlation with Child-Pugh score
authors: Jinhu Ma; Yan Ding; Haifeng Shao; Beiyu Zhang; Chunyu Jiang
abstract: BACKGROUND: Although two-dimensional speckle tracking imaging (2D-STI) enables sensitive and quantitative assessment of myocardial deformation, its application in patients with liver cirrhosis (LC) has largely been limited to ventricular function. This study applied 2D-STI to evaluate both ventricular and atrial function in order to identify early myocardial dysfunction in this population. METHODS: A total of 82 patients with LC were enrolled and stratified according to the Child-Pugh classification into Class A (n = 30), Class B (n = 29), and Class C (n = 23). Thirty healthy individuals served as controls. All 112 participants underwent conventional echocardiography and 2D-STI assessment. RESULTS: Compared with controls, all LC groups showed reduced left ventricular global longitudinal strain (LVGLS) and right ventricular free wall longitudinal strain (RVFWLS) (both P < 0.05), with a progressive decline from Class A to Class C. In contrast, right ventricular global longitudinal strain (RVGLS) was significantly decreased only in Classes B and C (P < 0.05). Left atrial conduit strain (LAScd) was significantly reduced across all LC groups (P < 0.05), whereas left atrial reservoir strain (LASr) and contractile strain (LASct) demonstrated a biphasic pattern -initially increased, then decreased- compared with controls. Overall, 2D-STI detected cardiac dysfunction earlier than conventional echocardiography. Significant negative correlations were observed between Child-Pugh score and LVGLS, RVFWLS, and RVGLS. CONCLUSION: Cardiac function is impaired in patients with LC and deteriorates with increasing disease severity. Compared with conventional echocardiography, 2D-STI detects cardiac dysfunction at an earlier stage, providing valuable support for early clinical intervention.

title: When Unilateral Pulmonary Edema Is Not Pneumonia: Fulminant Acute-on-Chronic Mitral Regurgitation Due to Spontaneous Chordal Rupture in Barlow’s Disease
authors: Nadia Loudiyi; Hafsa Erregui; Mohamed Malki; ZOUHAIR LAKHAL; Aatif Benyass
abstract: Unilateral pulmonary edema (UPE) is an uncommon and frequently overlooked manifestation of cardiogenic pulmonary edema that may mimic infectious pneumonia and is strongly associated with severe eccentric mitral regurgitation (MR), particularly in the setting of posterior leaflet prolapse or chordal rupture. We report the case of a 50-year-old woman with no previously known valvular heart disease who presented with abrupt-onset dyspnea at rest, rapidly progressing to severe respiratory distress and orthopnea within 24 hours. On admission, she was hypoxemic, with asymmetric crackles predominantly involving the right lung fields. Chest radiography demonstrated extensive right-sided alveolar infiltrates, initially raising suspicion of pneumonia. However, the absence of fever, systemic inflammatory response, and elevated infectious biomarkers prompted urgent cardiac evaluation. Transthoracic and transesophageal echocardiography revealed severe degenerative MR due to spontaneous chordal rupture, resulting in a flail P2 scallop extending into P3 on a background of Barlow’s disease, with a severe eccentric regurgitant jet. Despite initial stabilization with oxygen therapy, intravenous diuretics, and nitrates, the patient rapidly progressed to refractory cardiogenic shock requiring vasoactive and inotropic support. Urgent mitral valve surgery was indicated but could not be performed because of fulminant hemodynamic deterioration, and the patient died approximately two hours after admission to the cardiac intensive care unit. This case highlights a rare and catastrophic presentation of previously unrecognized degenerative MR in which spontaneous chordal rupture precipitated right-sided UPE and rapid hemodynamic collapse despite an apparently preserved left ventricular ejection fraction. It emphasizes that acute severe MR should be promptly considered in patients presenting with unilateral pulmonary infiltrates and acute respiratory failure when infectious features are absent. Early echocardiographic recognition and immediate surgical evaluation are crucial, as the therapeutic window before irreversible hemodynamic collapse may be extremely narrow.

title: Study of Left Ventricular Remodelling in Patients with Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease
authors: Mrutyunjay B. Hiregoudar; Dhananjaya M; Raghavendra Gangaraddy; Srinivas R
journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
abstract: This study aims to quantify left ventricular remodelling and the prevalence of left ventricular hypertrophy in patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease devoid of cardiovascular disease. It was a hospital based cross sectional includes adult patients diagnosed with COPD belonging to all classes of GOLD criteria which includes both OPD and IPD cases at SDMCMS&H. Patients with CAD, cardiomyopathy, LBBB , heart failure, significant valvular dysfunction , chronic AF, pacemaker , hypertension higher than stage1 and IDDM were excluded. Sample size is 150 . Thorough history , clinical examination , ECG , chest xray , echocardiography done. In the echocardiography interventricular septal wall thickness(SWT), posterior wall thickness (PWT) , left ventricular end diastolic diameter (EDD) , LVH noted. LVM and RWT calculated using appropriate formula . Results: In the present study , we noted that the mean age in the study was 70.24 years. In that 62% were males and 28% were females with male to female ratio of 1.63:1 . The mean SWT was 11.36mm , mean PWT- 11.15mm , mean LVEDD- 39.15mm. The RWT was below 0.42 in 4.67% of patients and above 0.42 in 95.33% subjects. Of the remodelling types observed 2% exhibited eccentric LVH and 98% concentric LVH. The average LVM – 202.87. CONCLUSION: By evaluating LVM and RWT, we aimed to quantify LV remodeling and the prevalence of LVH in COPD. The majority (95.33%) had a relative wall thickness greater than 0.42, with a high sensitivity (94.3%) and specificity (95.2%). Most subjects (98%) exhibited concentric LVH, and the left ventricular mass averaged 202.87, ranging from 62.10 to 529.63. These findings highlight significant demographic, clinical, and cardiac characteristics of the study population.

title: Infective Endocarditis Masked as Pulmonary Artery Thromboembolism – A Case Report
authors: NINO LEKVEISHVILI; Marina Kuparadze; Giorgi Imedashvili; Irina Lezhava; A Melia; TEIMURAZ MOSIAVA
abstract: Introduction. In people who inject drugs, infective endocarditis primarily affects the right side of the heart and often presents as septic pulmonary embolism. This clinical presentation can be easily misdiagnosed as pulmonary embolism, pneumonia, or primary cardiomyopathy, leading to delays in specific treatment. Case Description. A 50-year-old man who had been enrolled in a methadone maintenance program for four years was hospitalized with dyspnea at rest, orthopnea, fever, and lower-extremity edema; his oxygen saturation on room air was 85%. Echocardiography revealed dilation of all cardiac chambers, an ejection fraction of 18–20%, a pulmonary artery systolic pressure of 90 mmHg, and two mobile masses (17×8 mm and 17×7 mm) on the tricuspid valve leaflets. D-dimer levels exceeded 4000 ng/mL, and computed tomography angiography revealed bilateral segmental filling defects against a background of cavitating nodular lesions; the veins of the lower extremities were fully compressible. Antibiotic therapy remained empirical throughout, with the regimen changed three times. Despite 16 days of conservative treatment, fever, vegetations, and elevated inflammatory markers persisted, prompting the patient's transfer to a specialized clinic. There, preoperative echocardiography showed that the ejection fraction had already improved to 52%; coronary angiography ruled out hemodynamically significant coronary artery disease, and the tricuspid valve was replaced with a biological prosthesis. The patient was discharged in improved condition, and nine months later, heart failure corresponded to Functional Class II. Conclusion. Right-sided infective endocarditis should be considered in the differential diagnosis of any patient with a history of injection drug use, fever, and multiple focal pulmonary lesions-even when computed tomography shows filling defects in the pulmonary artery. Severe systolic dysfunction in these patients may be partially reversible and should not, in itself, be a reason to decline surgical intervention.

title: Pediatric Cardiac Surgery in the Pre-Conflict Era: A Retrospective Analysis of the Surgical patterns and outcomes Medani Heart Center, Sudan (2019–2022)
authors: Salah Hassan; Awab Mohieldeen; Mohamed Fargalla; Babekir Elmostafa; Yousry Mohammed
abstract: Abstract Background Pediatric cardiac care in sub-Saharan Africa is characterized by a significant surgical-medical gap, where late referrals and infrastructural limitations complicate outcomes for congenital and acquired heart disease. While Medani Heart Center (MHC) emerged as a critical tertiary referral hub in Sudan to address these geographic and systemic barriers, the 2023 conflict has fundamentally disrupted these specialized services. Documenting the clinical and procedural patterns established prior to this crisis is essential to providing a baseline for assessing current survival gaps and guiding future service restoration. This study evaluates the surgical patterns, patient demographics, and perioperative outcomes of pediatric cardiac patients managed at the MHC between 2019 and 2022. Methods We conducted a retrospective, observational cohort study of pediatric patients aged under 18 years who underwent cardiac surgical intervention at the Medani Heart Center (MHC), Sudan, between January 1, 2019, and December 31, 2022. Data were retrieved from the center’s official registry for 250 patients who met the inclusion criteria. Although the study was intended to extend into 2023, data from January 2023 onward were lost due to the destruction of the center's infrastructure during the national conflict. This analysis represents the final, verified clinical record of the MHC’s pediatric cardiac services prior to the suspension of operations. Results Among the 250 pediatric cardiac surgical patients analyzed, the majority were males (54.8%) and predominantly school-age children (54.0%). Procedures comprised structural congenital repairs (ventricular septal defect [VSD] 24.4%, atrial septal defect [ASD] 10.0%, patent ductus arteriosus [PDA] 9.2%), complex cyanotic anomaly corrections (Tetralogy of Fallot 18.8%), and valvular interventions (23.6%). Surgical volume peaked in 2021 (38.4%) before stabilizing in 2022. Post-operative outcomes were largely favorable, with 83.6% of patients experiencing an uneventful recovery and 87.2% requiring an intensive care unit (ICU) stay of 5 days or fewer. The overall mortality rate was 4.0%. Conclusion This study confirms that a high-volume regional pediatric cardiac surgical program can deliver efficient, high-quality care, evidenced by an 83.6% complication-free recovery rate and streamlined ICU management. The surge and subsequent stabilization of procedural volumes indicate a maturing clinical workflow capable of managing complex congenital and valvular cases. These findings validate the effectiveness of past clinical protocols while highlighting an essential baseline for future cardiovascular care reconstruction in the region. Clinical trial number: Not applicable.

title: Perioperative outcomes after aortic valve replacement via right anterior mini-thoracotomy with a rapid-deployment valve: a consecutive single-centre series
authors: Łukasz Jaworski; Krzysztof Jarmoszewicz; Marian Burysz; Sebastian Batkiewicz; Adam Ryszard Kowalówka; Michał Kuteń
abstract: Background/objectives Evidence for aortic valve replacement through right anterior thoracotomy (RAT) using the Edwards Intuity Elite rapid-deployment bioprosthesis remains limited, with only three dedicated single-centre series published to date. We aimed to describe perioperative safety, early haemodynamic performance, permanent pacemaker implantation for third-degree atrioventricular block, and new-onset postoperative atrial fibrillation in a consecutive single-centre cohort. Analyses of factors associated with these two rhythm endpoints were exploratory in nature. Methods This is a retrospective, single-arm, single-centre observational series with no sternotomy, ministernotomy or sutured-valve comparator. We analysed 70 consecutive patients undergoing isolated aortic valve replacement via RAT with the Edwards Intuity Elite bioprosthesis at a single institution. Percutaneous femoral arterial and venous cannulation was used in all cases. Outcomes were described for the whole cohort. For exploratory event-versus-no-event comparisons, Mann–Whitney U and Fisher's exact tests were applied to permanent pacemaker implantation and new-onset atrial fibrillation; Spearman rank correlation and Mann–Whitney U tests explored associations with operative times and discharge pressure gradients. Because only 6 pacemaker and 7 atrial fibrillation events occurred, statistical power was limited. Results Median age was 71.0 years and median EuroSCORE II was 1.0%. Median cross-clamp time was 61.0 min (IQR 54–75) and median cardiopulmonary bypass time was 103.5 min (IQR 84–115). In-hospital mortality was 1.4% (one death from femoral cannulation-site haemorrhage; 95% CI 0.0%–7.7%), and no strokes occurred. Permanent pacemaker implantation was required in 6 patients (8.6%; 95% CI 3.2–17.7%) and new-onset atrial fibrillation occurred in 7 (10.0%; 95% CI 4.1–19.5%); age was significantly associated with pacemaker implantation (median 75.5 vs. 71.0 years, p = 0.038), while other exploratory comparisons were not significant. No moderate or severe paravalvular leak was observed. Median postoperative mean gradient was 8.0 mmHg (IQR 6–10) and median length of stay was 6.0 days (IQR 6.0–7.0). Packed red blood cell transfusion was required in 63 patients (91.3% of 69 evaluable; 95% CI 82.0–96.7%), and reoperation for bleeding in 3 (4.3%; 95% CI 0.9–12.0%). Exploratory analyses detected no statistically significant association with atrial fibrillation or operative times. Implanted valve size correlated weakly and inversely with postoperative mean gradient (Spearman rho = −0.26, p = 0.032). Conclusions In this descriptive, low-risk, single-centre cohort, RAT with a rapid-deployment bioprosthesis was feasible and was followed by low discharge gradients. The observed pacemaker, atrial fibrillation, transfusion, bleeding and access-site event rates are real-world descriptive estimates and do not constitute comparative evidence of benefit over other approaches or prostheses. The small number of events precludes conclusions about predictors. Larger prospective multicentre studies with comparator groups and systematic echocardiographic follow-up are required.

title: Peripheral Artery Disease in Acute Care Settings: Diagnosis and Management of Common Presentations and Emergencies: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association
authors: Jennifer A. Rymer; Subhash Banerjee; Joshua Beckman; Abdulla A. Damluji; Katharine L. McGinigle; Lee Kirksey; Sahil Parikh; Alexander E. Sullivan; Debra Kohlman-Trigoboff; L. Wilkins; Eric Secemsky
abstract: People with peripheral artery disease (PAD) are often misdiagnosed or diagnosed late and, even after diagnosis, are undertreated with both pharmacologic and invasive therapies. The disease is associated with an increased risk of mortality, myocardial infarction, stroke, other vascular disease, limb loss, and reduced quality of life. Although the risks and long-term management of PAD are well documented, these risks are acutely magnified when PAD exists as a comorbidity in patients hospitalized for other cardiovascular or medical conditions. Procedures requiring vascular access for the treatment of acute myocardial infarction, cardiogenic shock, or valvular heart disease, as well as procedures for the treatment of the patient's underlying PAD, require special consideration in patients with PAD. Familiarity with the use and placement of mechanical circulatory support in patients with PAD, as well as the management of recent endovascular or surgical vascular interventions, is essential for providing appropriate care in the acute care setting.
